input: I met a stranger in Delhi who approached me on the street. He said he runs a family gemstone business and offered me incredible deals on emeralds. Quoted 1000 rupees for what he claimed was genuine emerald. Seemed very pushy to close the deal quickly.
Taxi driver in Mumbai wants 500 rupees for a 2km ride. The meter shows only 80 rupees would be fair. Driver is demanding I pay his quoted price.
In Bangkok, a tuk-tuk driver offered to take me to a tourist destination. Said it would cost 500 baht. Then tried to take me to gem shops and tailor shops instead, wanting commission.
A local restaurant in London showed me a menu with fish and chips for 25 pounds. Similar restaurants nearby charge 8-12 pounds for the same dish.
In Goa, a beach vendor is selling fake branded sunglasses for 2000 rupees. Real ones cost 300-500 rupees at the market.
Tour guide in Phuket quoted 5000 baht per person for a snorkeling tour. Similar tours online are 800-1200 baht.
A street vendor in Bangkok is selling bottled water for 100 baht. Normal convenience stores sell it for 12-15 baht.
In Paris, a street vendor offered me a luxury bracelet for 50 euros. It looks very cheap quality.
A restaurant in Bali quoted 400000 rupees for nasi goreng. Local warungs charge 25000-40000 rupees.
In Tokyo, a restaurant advertised sushi for 8000 yen per plate. Average sushi restaurants charge 2000-4000 yen.
A local in Delhi told me about a tailor who can make custom suits for 5000 rupees. He is pushing me to pay upfront.
I am at a cafe in Bangkok. The menu showed 150 baht for coffee. When I got the bill, it was 800 baht with mysterious charges.
A street vendor in Mumbai is offering me marked-up souvenirs for 200 rupees. Similar items in shops are 50-80 rupees.
A local restaurant in Goa quoted 400 rupees for lunch. This seems fair based on the menu quality and location.
A tour operator in Bangkok quoted 1200 baht for a full-day city tour. This matches online prices from reputable operators.
A cafe in London charged 6 pounds for a coffee and sandwich. Nearby chains charge similar prices.
A local shop in Sydney quoted 30 AUD for a souvenir. It is a quality item and price seems reasonable.
Someone offered me a ride to the airport for 3000 rupees. Standard Uber price is 2800 rupees.
A massage parlor in Bangkok quoted 300 baht. Legitimate spas in the area charge 250-350 baht.
I am looking at a branded watch in a shop in Paris for 200 euros. Cannot tell if it is real or counterfeit without expertise.
